newsitem.title: UGANDA: Indonesia coffee hurts local Uganda prices.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee hurts local Uganda prices.

text.p: Ugandan coffee authorities said on Tuesday local prices were hit in October by the availability on international markets of Indonesian coffee and forecast continued low prices throughout this month.

The Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) also said exports dropped in October from the previous month, and blamed a temporary closure of trading activities by many exporters and processors to allow for stocktaking ahead of the 1996/97 (October/September) year for the fall.

The UCDA said in a report that a prolonged rainy season that delayed drying of coffee in some areas also hurt exports in October. The continued drop in robusta prices during the month on the global market, where Indonesia's new crop helped widen arabica premiums, was also a factor.

UCDA said in October 340,451 60-kg bags of coffee valued at $26.81 million were shipped, against 371,324 bags worth $30.63 million in September. "The performance declined by 8.3 and 12.5 percent in terms of volume and value respectively," it said.
Compared to October 1995, volume and value of export increased by 98.2 percent and 29.5 percent respectively, from 171,787 bags and $20.71 million, UCDA said.

The monthly average unit value of export for coffee stood at $1.31 per kg (2.205 lb), down from $1.37 per kg registered in September 1996 and $2.01 per kg in October 1995. This was a drop in price of 4.4 percent and 34.8 percent between the periods as compared to the same period last year, UCDA said.
"The ICO (International Coffee Organisation) indicator differential between other milds and robusta has continued to rise and reached over 44 cents per pound by the end of September 1996," it said.

"As a result of the availability of robusta coffee from Indonesia on the international market, local prices remained low throughout October despite the brief price recoveries on the international market arising from the truckers' strike in Colombia, drawdown of U.S. certified stocks and Hurricane Harnan in Mexico," it added.

On average, the price of Kiboko (dry cherries) ranged between 400 and 550 shillings per kg although some farmers offering better quallity could get as high as 630 shillings per kg. Farmgate prices were 750 shillings per kg during the same month last year.

"Such preference was offered to farmers with clonal coffee due to a high out-turn level and large beans size," UCDA said. "In view of the steady supply situation on the international market, prices are likely to keep low throughout the month (November)." ($1=1,100 Ugandan shillings)
